topics.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: know that a force is a push or a pull and that the unit of force is the Newton (k)
know the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on objects (k, s)

body.text: A force is a push or a pull that one object exerts on another. The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

When two or more forces act on an object, they can be combined into a single resultant force that has the same overall effect. Forces acting in the same direction add together; forces acting in opposite directions subtract from each other.

When the forces acting on an object are balanced — their resultant is zero — the object's motion does not change: it stays at rest, or keeps moving at a constant speed in a straight line. When the forces are unbalanced — a non-zero resultant force acts — the object's motion changes: it speeds up, slows down, or changes direction.
Use the PhET Forces and Motion: Basics simulation below (Net Force screen). Apply pushes and pulls to the cart and watch how balanced and unbalanced forces change — or fail to change — its motion.
